parsed_answer.content:
The main method in Java acts as the absolute entry point for any standalone standard application execution. When looking at its precise signature, public static void main(String[] args), every modifier carries strict semantic meaning enforced by the Java Virtual Machine (JVM). The public access modifier allows the JVM launcher—running outside the class—to invoke the method regardless of package boundaries. The static keyword tells the JVM that it can execute this method without instantiating an object of the containing class, which is vital since the application hasn't initialized any objects yet. The return type void indicates that the method does not return a value back to the operating system or runtime launcher. Finally, the String[] args parameter array provides a mechanism to pass command-line arguments directly into the application runtime, enabling configuration or input injection at startup.

When you execute a Java class from the command line using the java command, a sophisticated chain of events triggers beneath the surface. First, the OS invokes the native Java launcher executable (java or java.exe), which subsequently bootstraps the JVM instance by loading the HotSpot runtime via dynamic link libraries. Once the JVM is initialized, the Bootstrap Class Loader, followed by the Extension and Application Class Loaders, locates and loads the target byte code file (.class) from the classpath. The bytecode verifier inspects the instructions for structural and security violations before the Just-In-Time (JIT) compiler or interpreter takes over. The JVM then searches specifically for a method matching the exact main signature. Upon discovery, it creates the initial main thread, pushes the main stack frame onto the thread's execution stack, and begins executing bytecode instructions sequentially.

items: The JVM thread scheduler initializes the main thread, allocating native OS thread resources and a dedicated JVM stack memory region.
System properties and environment variables are bound to the runtime context before the class initializer (<clinit>) blocks execute.
Bytecode verification ensures type safety and prevents malicious code from subverting JVM memory safety guarantees prior to execution.
The String[] array passed to main is constructed dynamically from space-delimited tokens provided on the command line interface.

parsed_answer.content: A common production gotcha involves classpath resolution issues when running classes from the command line. If your class uses external libraries or packages, forgetting to specify the -cp or --class-path flag with the correct directory structure will throw a ClassNotFoundException or NoClassDefFoundError before the main method is even reached. Additionally, remember that main must be explicitly named 'main'; changing the casing or misspelling it results in a runtime error stating that the main method is not found in the class.
